gloss: complete stranger; total stranger; person with no connection whatsoever

definitions.explanation: A person with absolutely no connection or relationship to oneself. Emphasizes the complete lack of any bond, acquaintance, or relation.

examples.japanese: ⟦{私|わたし}→私：02988_watashi⟧⟦にとって→にとって：06803_nitotte⟧⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧{赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}だ。
examples.english: To me, he is now a complete stranger.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{助|たす}けて→助ける：00895_tasukeru⟧⟦もらった→もらう：00520_morau⟧。
examples.english: I was helped by a complete stranger.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{親切|しんせつ}→親切：01144_shinsetsu⟧にして⟦くれた→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: Even though we were total strangers, they were kind to me.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ here is an intensifier meaning "completely" or "utterly" (not the color red). This use of ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ appears in other expressions like {赤|あか}っ{恥|ぱじ} (utter embarrassment) and ⟦{赤裸々|せきらら}→赤裸々：17380_sekirara⟧ (frank, completely bare).

USAGE:
Stronger than just ⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧ (stranger). Emphasizes:
- Complete absence of any relationship
- No blood ties, friendship, or acquaintance
- Used when severing ties or emphasizing distance
- Expressing that someone is/has become irrelevant to you
- Describing unexpected kindness from strangers
- Discussing family estrangement
- Contrasting relationships (family vs. strangers)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ - to become complete strangers
- {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{同然|どうぜん}→同然：09487_douzen⟧ - practically a stranger
- {赤|あか}の{他人|たにん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{頼|たよ}る→頼る：02069_tayoru⟧ - to rely on a complete stranger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{見|み}ず{知|し}らず→見ず知らず：07456_mizushirazu⟧ - total stranger
- {行|ゆ}きずり - passerby, chance encounter
- ⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧ - stranger, other person (less emphatic)
- ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧ - person one doesn't know
